57700-toronto-by-gaslight-the-night-hawk.creator: Unknown
57700-toronto-by-gaslight-the-night-hawk.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Night has fallen over the city. The hum of a hundred industries which make the daytime resonant with the whirr of wheels, the clank of hammers, and the throb of huge engines, is silent. Deserted are the factories and workshops and warehouses, where a few hours ago all was life and stir in the eager struggle for subsistence. arxiv-2008-12771.title: Parallel entangling gate operations and two-way quantum communication in spin chains
arxiv-2008-12771.creator: Rozhin Yousefjani, Abolfazl Bayat
arxiv-2008-12771.description: Abstract The power of a quantum circuit is determined through the number of two-qubit entangling gates that can be performed within the coherence time of the system. In the absence of parallel quantum gate operations, this would make the quantum simulators limited to shallow circuits.

arxiv-2202-09793.title: Controlling nonautonomous matter waves in “smart” transient trap variations
arxiv-2202-09793.creator: S. Sree Ranjani, Tangirala Shreecharan, Thokala Soloman Raju
arxiv-2202-09793.description: Abstract In this paper, we study the controllable behavior of nonautonomous matter waves in different “smart” transient trap variations in the context of the cigar-shaped Bose-Einstein condensates. By utilizing a self-similarity transformation we reduce the nonautonomous Gross-Pitaevskii (GP) equation to the elliptic equation that admits soliton solutions.

arxiv-2203-10798.title: Generating series of classes of exotic un-ordered configuration spaces
arxiv-2203-10798.creator: Sabir M. Gusein-Zade
arxiv-2203-10798.description: Abstract A notion of exotic (ordered) configuration spaces of points on a space X X was suggested by Yu. Baryshnikov. He gave equations for the (exponential) generating series of the Euler characteristics of these spaces. Here we consider un-ordered analogues of these spaces.

arxiv-2211-06925.title: Early Diagnosis of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease from Chest X-Rays using Transfer Learning and Fusion Strategies
arxiv-2211-06925.creator: Ryan Wang, Li-Ching Chen, Lama Moukheiber, Mira Moukheiber, Dana Moukheiber, Zach Zaiman, Sulaiman Moukheiber, Tess Litchman, Kenneth Seastedt, Hari Trivedi, Rebecca Steinberg, Po-Chih Kuo, Judy Gichoya, Leo Anthony Celi
arxiv-2211-06925.description: Abstract Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is one of the most common chronic illnesses in the world and the third leading cause of mortality worldwide but is often underdiagnosed. COPD is difficult to diagnose early and often is not diagnosed until later in the disease course.

arxiv-2301-13514.title: Fourier Sensitivity and Regularization of Computer Vision Models
arxiv-2301-13514.creator: Kiran Krishnamachari kirank@u.nus.edu, See-Kiong Ng seekiong@nus.edu.sg, Chuan-Sheng Foo foo_chuan_sheng@i2r.a-star.edu.sg
arxiv-2301-13514.description: Abstract Recent work has empirically shown that deep neural networks latch on to the Fourier statistics of training data and show increased sensitivity to Fourier-basis directions in the input. Understanding and modifying this Fourier-sensitivity of computer vision models may help improve their robustness.

arxiv-2407-08731.title: Massive-ish Particles from Small-ish Scales: Non-Perturbative Techniques for Cosmological Collider Physics from Large-Scale Structure Surveys
arxiv-2407-08731.creator: Samuel Goldstein, Oliver H. E. Philcox, J. Colin Hill, Lam Hui
arxiv-2407-08731.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Samuel Goldstein, Oliver H. E. Philcox, J. Colin Hill, Lam Hui. Massive particles produced during inflation impact soft limits of primordial correlators. Searching for these signatures presents an exciting opportunity to uncover the particle spectrum in the inflationary epoch. We present non-perturbative methods to constrain intermediate-mass scalars ( 0 ≤ m / H < 3 / 2 0\leq m/H<3/2 , where H H is the inflationary Hubble scale) produced during inflation, which give rise to a power-law scaling in the squeezed primordial bispectrum.

Malignant tumor, one of the most threatening diseases to human health, has been comprehensively treated with surgery, radiotherapy, chemotherapy and targeted therapy, but the prognosis has not always been ideal. In the past decade, immunotherapy has shown increased efficacy in tumor treatment; however, for immunotherapy to achieve its fullest potential, obstacles are to be conquered, among which tumor microenvironment (TME) has been widely investigated.

pmc-11577905.title: Gut metatranscriptomics based de novo assembly reveals microbial signatures predicting immunotherapy outcomes in non-small cell lung cancer
pmc-11577905.creator: David Dora, Peter Kiraly, Csenge Somodi, Balazs Ligeti, Edit Dulka, Gabriella Galffy, Zoltan Lohinai
pmc-11577905.description: BackgroundAdvanced-stage non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) poses treatment challenges, with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) as the main therapy. Emerging evidence suggests the gut microbiome significantly influences ICI efficacy. This study explores the link between the gut microbiome and ICI outcomes in NSCLC patients, using metatranscriptomic (MTR) signatures.

pmc-12433048.creator: Jingjing Ren, Shengyan Qu, Keyun Bian, Min Yao, Fan Yao, Feifan Xu, Rui Zhang
pmc-12433048.description: BackgroundUnlike smear-positive tuberculosis (TB) which is more easily diagnosed due to the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) in sputum, smear-negative pulmonary tuberculosis (SN-TB) poses a diagnostic challenge that can lead to delayed treatment hence new molecular diagnostic markers are urgently needed.

pmc-12487744.title: Oxidation‐Enhanced Piezocatalytic Activity in Carbon Nitride‐Based Catalysts for Hydrogen and Hydrogen Peroxide Production
pmc-12487744.creator: Ying Pan, Luocheng Liao, Xinwen Zhang, Yunya Liu, Ran Su, Nieves López‐Salas
pmc-12487744.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Driven by the urgent need for a green, safe, and cost‐effective approach to producing H2 and H2O2—both highly valuable in green energy and environmental protection fields—piezocatalysis, which converts mechanical energy into valuable chemicals, has emerged as a promising solution. However, current catalyst systems face challenges due to the need for materials with both a strong piezoelectric effect and favorable catalytic activity. Herein, the construction of an oxidized carbon nitride (g‐C3N4) matrix anchored with TiO2 nanoparticles via alkaline hydrothermal treatment is reported.

pmc-12722753.title: Construction and validation of a novel model for guiding targeted combined immunotherapy in advanced hepatocellular carcinoma
pmc-12722753.creator: Haibin Tu, Siyi Feng, Lihong Chen, Yujie Huang, Juzhen Zhang, Suyu Peng, Dingluan Lin, Xiaojian Ye
pmc-12722753.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). In addressing the challenge of optimizing targeted combined immunotherapy for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), this study developed and validated a novel prognostic model, the Target Immunotherapy Predict Model (TIPM), utilizing ultrasound and serological markers. Data from patients at Mengchao Hepatobiliary Hospital and Fujian Provincial Cancer Hospital were analyzed, encompassing demographics, serological markers, and ultrasound findings, including tumor and peritumoral tissue stiffness changes pre- and post-treatment.

pmc-13072257.title: Mitogenomic Analysis and Conservation Genetics of the Endangered Oriental Stork (Ciconia boyciana)
pmc-13072257.creator: Xiao-Die Chen, Yun-Yun Wang, Zhi-Min Xu, Lin Xiao, Chang-Hu Lu, Cheng-He Sun, Cheng-Zhi Li
pmc-13072257.description: Simple SummaryThe Oriental Stork (Ciconia boyciana) is a rare wetland bird currently listed as Endangered on the IUCN Red List. While it is a flagship species for conservation, there has been a significant lack of up-to-date mitochondrial genomic data from its core habitats in mainland China.

pmc-13200720.title: Gut yeasts accelerate chill coma recovery in Drosophila melanogaster
pmc-13200720.creator: Yanira Jiménez-Padilla, Brent J. Sinclair
pmc-13200720.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The role of microbial symbionts in host stress tolerance remains underexplored. Gut microbiome studies in Drosophila melanogaster have largely focused on bacteria, whereas yeasts have been assumed to provide nutrition rather than engage in true symbiosis. We explored the effect of gut yeasts on chill coma recovery time (CCRT, a proxy for cold tolerance) and its yeast species-specificity and dependence on live yeast cells.

pmc-13581142.description: BackgroundCisgender college women are vulnerable to HIV transmission but rarely use biomedical prevention tools such as pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP).
